page: Amazon Web Services g4ad.16xlarge is a graphics-intensive server instance powered by the AWS Nitro hypervisor. It features an AMD EPYC 7R32 processor with 64 vCPUs and 32 physical cores running at 3.0 GHz on the x86_64 architecture. The hardware configuration includes 256.0 GB of DDR4 memory operating at 3 GHz, providing 4.0 GB of RAM per core. For graphics and parallel computing workloads, the instance is equipped with four AMD Radeon Pro Navi V520 GPUs delivering a total of 32 GB of VRAM. Local storage consists of 2400 GB of NVMe SSD capacity, and the network interface provides a baseline bandwidth of 25 Gbps.

Benchmark data reveals a contrast between single-core and multi-core performance. The stress-ng single-core CPU performance is categorized as poor, and the Geekbench single-core score is average. However, multi-core and specialized execution show stronger results. The Passmark CPU score, extended instructions test, and encryption test are all rated as strong. Ray tracing performance via Geekbench is also strong. Memory performance is robust, with a strong Passmark memory score and average read and write bandwidths. Large-model LLM text generation using a 70B model is a notable bottleneck, scoring in the weak category, while smaller model inference remains average.

From a qualitative cost-efficiency perspective, the g4ad.16xlarge offers a dense allocation of four GPUs and local NVMe storage bundled with a high vCPU count, making it a resource-dense option for parallel processing without requiring ultra-premium enterprise AI accelerators. The instance is suited for graphics-intensive applications, ray tracing, multi-threaded decompression, and database operations. It is also appropriate for moderate LLM inference and software compilation, though it is less optimal for workloads heavily dependent on single-core CPU speed.
